text: “What a strange thing!” said the overseer of the workmen at the foundry. “This broken lead heart will not melt in the furnace. We must throw it away.” So they threw it on a dust-heap where the dead Swallow was also lying. “Bring me the two most precious things in the city,” said God to one of His Angels; and the Angel brought Him the leaden heart and the dead bird. “You have rightly chosen,” said God, “for in my garden of Paradise this little bird shall sing for evermore, and in my city of gold the Happy Prince shall praise me.”
title: The Foundry Heap
director_note: I staged the ruin as a warm, flickering foundry scene, letting the dead swallow lie still while the angel descends, gathers the leaden heart and bird, and rises away into light. The final ascent turns loss into praise by carrying both precious things upward together.
